scope: Phase1 assigned nine one-off generators; local source/repair/archive review, no new live DB queries or generator execution. All nine accounted for.

cases.title: Determining an intercept of an implicit tangent or normal
cases.intended_learner_operation: Differentiate implicitly, evaluate the slope, choose tangent/normal, recall a line equation, and infer the requested axis intercept.
cases.defective_behavior: Easy prompts appended the point-slope formula and the axis-zero reminder, removing independent prerequisite recall from ordinary practice.
cases.literal_interpretation_or_proxy: Easy was explicitly implemented as supported practice, with moderate distinguished by removing support. Tutorial/example steps were treated as warrant for supplying those steps before response.
cases.semantic_loss: The activity changed from independently assembling the derivative-to-intercept chain to completing a partially prescribed procedure; preserving the final answer and algebra did not preserve independence.
cases.repair: Removed formula and axis reminder; kept arithmetic, banks and moderate/hard output. Shared prompt contradiction was explicitly repaired.
cases.evidence_strength: Direct authored rationale + original runtime + later repair. Link to a particular instruction is documented by the repair README; mental state is not inferred.

evidence.supports: Tutorial and example stages cited as evidence.
Explicit easy point-slope/axis support and moderate no scaffold.
Actual easy-only hint branch.
Contradictory reduced-support instruction replaced.
Repair restores full learner chain.

cases.counterevidence_or_other_cause: The old author correctly articulated the full target at instructional-account.md:3 and had already restored differentiation after an earlier scaffold. This is a failure to enforce a stated purpose across all stages, not evidence of zero understanding.

cases.title: Multiplying 3x3 square matrices
cases.intended_learner_operation: Locate the left row and right column for each requested product entry, pair and multiply, sum, and place the result.
cases.defective_behavior: Every easy item supplied a row/column reminder and one fully selected dot-product setup.
cases.literal_interpretation_or_proxy: Source partial output matrices plus a requirement for easy/moderate/hard progression were expanded into pre-answer method support: three blanks with one setup versus five unaided versus nine unaided.
cases.semantic_loss: Supplying nonrequested results reduces repetition; supplying the dot product performs an assessed selection decision. The implementation treated these two kinds of assistance as interchangeable.
cases.repair: Removed both method reminder and selected dot product while retaining partial matrices and the numerical/entry-count progression.
cases.evidence_strength: Direct historical instructional account, accepted review and archived code. The review positively endorses the later-removed assistance.

evidence.supports: Author correctly identifies locating/pairing as the target.
Easy gives one setup, leaving two independent pairings.
Accepted review describes support removal as progression.
Actual hint construction.
Imported partial matrices give results, not dot-product setups.

cases.counterevidence_or_other_cause: Partial matrices themselves are supported and remain after repair. The author/reviewer understood the calculation and tested substantial correctness; the loss concerns where learner decisions occur, not mathematical correctness.

cases.title: Calculating an initial amount
cases.intended_learner_operation: Set up continuous compounding with the correct sign/duration, solve for the initial amount, evaluate and round once.
cases.defective_behavior: Distractors were small random offsets around the rounded key, admitting 2.55 beside the correct 2.54.
cases.literal_interpretation_or_proxy: Generate five distinct nearby choices while covering all five numerical key ranks. Numerical separation and rank diversity became the practical acceptance target.
cases.semantic_loss: The item can turn on incidental rounding rather than the modeled calculation; arbitrary jitter does not represent mistakes in the intended method.
cases.repair: Use plausible sign, duration, percentage and simple-interest errors; reject insufficient spacing, retain precision to final rounding, treat requested rank as a preference.
cases.evidence_strength: Direct generator code proves rank-conditioned random offsets; historical review rewards rank coverage; causal instruction-following mechanism is an interpretation of that alignment, not a quoted original command.

evidence.supports: Random offsets limited by 2.5% and allocated above/below according to requested rank.
Review permits independent correct-choice rank/position variation.
All five ranks explicitly used as evidence.
Reported 2.54/2.55 failure and wider imported spacing.
Repair and rank preference limitation.

cases.counterevidence_or_other_cause: The key and high-precision arithmetic were correct. This is distractor design, not a rounding bug. Source replay itself was valid.

cases.title: Calculating a rate or time duration
cases.intended_learner_operation: Invert continuous compounding using logarithms, handle units/percent conversion, and round the requested rate or time.
cases.defective_behavior: Independently sampled integer answer banks could contain adjacent years or percentage points.
cases.literal_interpretation_or_proxy: Bank-first sampling and feasibility inversion removed rank/midpoint clues, while five distinct values were treated as sufficient spacing.
cases.semantic_loss: A bank can resist simple choice-only shortcuts and still impose finer numerical discrimination than the intended source family.
cases.repair: Keep bank-first design but require imported-family spacing of two years or three percentage points.
cases.evidence_strength: Direct archived bank sampler and accepted review; no claim that the author consciously prioritized metrics over meaning.

evidence.supports: Sorted random sample of five integers, no minimum gaps.
Accepted same-bank all-key/midpoint counterexample tests.
Adjacent-integer issue and family-specific spacing repair.

cases.counterevidence_or_other_cause: The bank-first repair addresses a real prior shortcut and is retained. The failure is an omitted additional constraint, not evidence that counterfactual testing is unhelpful.

cases.title: Calculating a final amount after continuous compounding
cases.intended_learner_operation: Apply continuous compounding with correct signed rate and time units, then round the final amount.
cases.defective_behavior: No defective existing bank was established in this episode. The generator lacked the new spacing guarantee and received preventive hardening.
cases.literal_interpretation_or_proxy: Old code generates wrong values below/above the key according to a sampled rank and checks only distinctness; this is a latent design exposure rather than an observed served failure.
cases.semantic_loss: Potential for adjacent rounded options, but the five existing final-amount questions already passed the new spacing requirement.
cases.repair: Add common amount-spacing guard for future draws; preserve all five existing questions and moderate-only scope.
cases.evidence_strength: Direct archived code and explicit repair summary counterevidence. Do not count this as an observed pedagogical failure.

evidence.supports: Rank-conditioned random alternatives and distinctness check.
All five valid final-amount questions preserved.
Existing banks already passed; guard added for future draws.

cases.counterevidence_or_other_cause: This is the clearest warning against equating modified generators with demonstrated failures.

cases.title: Finding triangle area given quadrilateral area
cases.intended_learner_operation: Identify the enclosing triangle, compute its area from two sides and included angle using sine, then subtract the given quadrilateral area.
cases.defective_behavior: An older item supplied both areas. A subsequent repair restored area calculation but kept right angles throughout easy/moderate and supplied the easy method.
cases.literal_interpretation_or_proxy: Preserve two visible operations and distinguish levels by removing a hint, then add nonright-angle calculation only in hard.
cases.semantic_loss: Restoring an area multiplication was treated as preserving the full target; easy/moderate still bypassed the sine-area decision. A nominally complete operation count missed which operation the lesson teaches.
cases.repair: All bands retain sine-area calculation and subtraction; modest numerical changes control demand without hints or extra skills.
cases.evidence_strength: Direct old account and accepted review explicitly describe the deficient progression; archival runtime confirms right-angle sampling and hint.

evidence.supports: Literal progression with hint removal and sine only hard; calls prior subtraction-only repair corrected.
Reviewer accepts guided easy and general-angle hard.
Reviewer verifies hints render bold.
Explicit easy hint.
All nonhard angles fixed at90.
Canonical and imported evidence; no easy/moderate anchors.
Same sine-area/subtract task in all bands.

cases.counterevidence_or_other_cause: A right-angle imported example is legitimate; the failure is making it the whole easy/moderate family. No imported easy/moderate calibration existed. The author had done substantive geometry/source review, so claim partial objective preservation rather than no understanding.

cases.title: Calculating a matrix product using the distributive law
cases.intended_learner_operation: Recognize a common matrix factor and simplify in the correct order, filling requested product entries in the source partial-matrix format.
cases.defective_behavior: Unrequested cells were replaced by asterisks instead of the source-supported numerical entries.
cases.literal_interpretation_or_proxy: A partial answer matrix was interpreted as an API distinction between input and noninput cells; unrequested cells were treated as irrelevant and hidden.
cases.semantic_loss: The response schema remained valid but the learner-facing mathematical presentation changed. Source-supported partial matrices were generalized to an invented notation without examining why supplied entries were present.
cases.repair: Always display actual unrequested entries and use the source missing-entry phrasing; retain operands, target cells, keys and solutions.
cases.evidence_strength: Direct original code and full source audit establish authored presentation departure. The API/intent explanation is inferred; no original agent statement of motive located.

evidence.supports: supplied_entries defaults false.
Unrequested cells default to ast; real entries optional.
All21 sources reviewed; none use asterisks;9 numerical partial matrices.
Underlying distributive structure supported.
Presentation-only repair preserving mathematical structure.

cases.counterevidence_or_other_cause: This does not prove the question became harder or leaked an answer. Arithmetic/distributive-law structure was valid; it is source-format/learner-presentation drift.

cases.title: Graphing a curve defined parametrically
cases.intended_learner_operation: Evaluate parameter checkpoints and distinguish the corresponding curve using readable coordinates and shapes.
cases.defective_behavior: Translated/shared-checkpoint distractors required one-unit discrimination, while automatic ticks produced three-unit grids; mathematically distinct loci could be hard to distinguish at actual display size.
cases.literal_interpretation_or_proxy: Plot correctness was treated as fitting all curves, shared bounds/equal aspect, integer ticks, and distinct loci. Increasing tick count was used without measuring whether the assessed visual difference could be read.
cases.semantic_loss: The practice shifted from mathematical graph recognition to visual interpolation/estimation. A correct plot specification in coordinates did not preserve a usable perceptual task.
cases.repair: Bank-wide common readable grid/display policy; reject unresolved variants; unmarked answer curves versus calculated dots in solution; actual pixel/phone checks.
cases.evidence_strength: Direct original renderer, recorded audit and accepted progression review. Literal conversion of plot requirements is a supported mechanism inference; no claim of original motive.

evidence.supports: One-unit distractor translation versus3-unit grid.
Extent/layout algorithm rather than assessed distinction.
Task shift toward closer loci without matching readability validation.
MaxNLocator9 integer ticks.
Original accepted progression explicitly uses translations and shared endpoints.
Reject unresolved variants at240px.

cases.counterevidence_or_other_cause: Shared scale/equal aspect prevent answer cues and remain useful. Coarse grids are valid for some imported broad-shape tasks; a universal1-unit rule would repeat the same context loss.

cases.title: Identifying equilibrium solutions of an ODE
cases.intended_learner_operation: Recall the constant-solution criterion, respect the original domain, rearrange once when needed, and test each proposed constant in the same residual.
cases.defective_behavior: Moderate sampling added the same arbitrary linear term to both sides solely to cancel; solution expanded useful shifted structure then abandoned residual form for repeated L/R checks. Easy supplied the criterion; hard could become domain-only selection.
cases.literal_interpretation_or_proxy: Difficulty progression was operationalized as supplying criterion in easy, requiring recall/rearrangement in moderate, adding a domain decision in hard. Formal extra steps and preserved checkbox shape stood in for coherent target reasoning.
cases.semantic_loss: Moderate gained artificial algebraic workload; feedback obscured the compact target test. Easy removed recall; a hard bank where every valid candidate is correct replaces equilibrium testing with domain recognition.
cases.repair: Remove cancelling wrappers/criterion hints, retain factored residual throughout, and require both excluded and valid non-equilibrium hard candidates.
cases.evidence_strength: Direct archived code/audit and accepted review. The review expressly says all retain the same checkbox identification task despite different required reasoning.

evidence.supports: Manufactured wrapper, expansion and method switch.
Accepted progression supplies criterion then removes support; equates shared checkbox task with retained objective.
L/R presentation was itself a fix for clipped substitution, showing a local repair tradeoff.
Repairs wrappers, residual structure, criterion and domain-only banks.
No imported moderate/hard anchors; legitimate source logarithm follows residual.

cases.counterevidence_or_other_cause: Original banks were correctly keyed, logarithms were legitimate source material, and some L/R changes solved real layout problems. This is a coherent-method and workload failure, not incorrect equilibrium mathematics.

patterns.pattern: Support removal substituted for difficulty while changing independent practice
patterns.finding: Historical authors and reviewers often state the right target, then accept hints as a way to manufacture band separation. The evidence supports a failure to enforce the intent, not necessarily a failure to articulate it.

patterns.pattern: Technical/proxy success treated as preservation of the task
patterns.finding: Five distinct choices, diverse key ranks, valid partial fields, correct plot loci and unchanged checkbox type are all properties of the artifact, not sufficient evidence of what the learner must do.

patterns.pattern: Local repair changes one symptom while leaving or creating another
patterns.finding: Restoring an area step still bypassed sine; restoring differentiation retained line hints; bank-first sampling fixed midpoint clues but lacked spacing; shorter L/R feedback lost coherent residual method; integer ticks did not guarantee readable spacing.

patterns.pattern: Sparse difficulty anchors encouraged authored progression without checking target continuity
patterns.finding: Records honestly label missing easy or higher-band anchors; being explicit that a band is authored did not make its design faithful to independent practice.

patterns.pattern: Modified package is not proof of failure
patterns.finding: Final-amount banks already passed; this episode added a preventive future guard. Exclude it from observed-failure numerator.

causal_limit: Runtime behavior, authored rationale and prior accepted review judgments are directly documented. Claims about the original agents cognitive process or literal instruction causation require the parent historical-prompt comparison; current postrepair prompts were not used as proof of original instruction.
